subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Surfside Condo Collapse in Florida
description: A quick, practical guide to The Surfside Condo Collapse in Florida.

hook.text: On June 24, 2021, half of Champlain Towers South in Surfside, Florida, collapsed without warning at 1:22 AM. 98 people died.

buildup.text: A 2018 engineering report found major structural damage in the pool deck and garage. Repairs were estimated at $15 million.

discovery.text: Water pooled on the flat pool deck for decades. It seeped through cracks, corroding rebar until the concrete lost its support.

twist.text: Residents argued over the cost of repairs for three years. The building collapsed before work could begin.

climax.text: Florida now requires structural inspections every 25 years for buildings near the coast, with recertification every 10 years.

punchline.text: The report was filed. The repairs were debated. Time ran out.

quiz.question: What was the primary cause of the Surfside condo collapse?
options: An earthquake destabilized the foundation pilings under the building
Water infiltration corroded the rebar under the pool deck, weakening the concrete
The building exceeded its designed lifespan and should have been demolished
